panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — At the one-day-early vibration check, Zib works on the maintenance fan with Jax holding the access tag and route slate. Zib warns them not to hurry for headquarters' star.
PANEL 2 — Jax looks up from the isolated equipment and makes his lunch joke; Mira's sample reader is not yet the frame's focus.
PANEL 3 — Mira records the first vibration reading and notes that a measurement is not a reward. The slightly loose mount can be seen beside her instrument.
PANEL 4 — Zib tightens the conventional mount and restores the fan; Pixa verifies that the completed check is within operating limits.
PANEL 5 — An ordinary passive sample appears near the work area. Astra looks to Mira for interpretation without claiming it proves the output target.
PANEL 6 — At the operations display Pixa posts TARGET PROGRESS: 19% while Mira cautions Astra that the new sample's cause is unknown. The number must not dominate the technical reality.
PANEL 1 — At Dock 2, Jax sees an early arrival notice while the conveyor is still isolated and service panels are open across the loading lane.
PANEL 2 — Zib confirms the conveyor cannot take cargo through the isolated lane; Jax keeps barriers and access tags in place.
PANEL 3 — Mira logs the interlock readings beside the stopped equipment, keeping the physical repair separate from the optional collection result.
PANEL 4 — Pixa gives Astra an updated estimate from actual conditions while Zib checks the conveyor and finds no major fault. No invented success display.
PANEL 5 — A modest residue sample appears near the warm motor housing. Astra warns the crew not to let the pilot output target change the maintenance steps.
PANEL 6 — Pixa updates TARGET PROGRESS: 31%. Jax, looking from that number toward the arriving-cargo notice, insists they finish properly despite having started early.

summary: The early Dock 2 conveyor outage is real, even though the passive-collection target is tempting. Jax manages arriving cargo, Zib keeps isolation safe, Mira captures measurements, Pixa reports only a bounded estimate and Astra refuses to change the repair to chase a sample.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Standing beside the real work board, Astra tells the small group that she moved the conveyor work early and cost Dock 2 time. Avoid a posed seven-person review tableau.
PANEL 2 — Zib, beside Astra and the maintenance ticket, confirms that the fault was real but the early schedule was a choice. Other staff need not occupy the panel.
PANEL 3 — Jax points to the actual dock-delay record rather than a target graph; he wants no more schedules built around lucky samples.
PANEL 4 — At the report station, Kreeb and Glorp distinguish properly done work from a report designed to look impressive. Glorp preserves both the repair and the bad timing in the causal record.
PANEL 5 — Pixa files the unvarnished report as Astra watches, the incoming eleven-minute delay visible but not rebranded as an abstract benchmark problem.

summary: Astra owns her decision to accelerate Dock 2 service and the resulting delay. Zib and Jax name the practical consequence, Kreeb and Glorp distinguish honest work from an attractive report, and Pixa records the accurate account instead of a target-friendly version.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Pixa shows the central review response: BENCHMARK NOT MET / PILOT STATUS REVIEW SCHEDULED, with a choice of additional collection for the target or an alternate operating proposal.
PANEL 2 — Astra declines the extra output-driven shift and selects the factual operating-proposal option, remembering the failed accelerated maintenance schedule.

PANEL 3 — Astra turns from the benchmark to the real station work board and begins describing actual service, repair and evidence practices. End on a clear document-in-progress, not another target score.

summary: Central offers either more target-chasing or a different station operating proposal. Astra rejects another collection shift and begins writing what the station really does, rather than another output-driven schedule.
